subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@acme.com>, Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & next steps

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned. I’ve included Vivek and Dev on this thread for the technical deep dive.

Summary of what we heard (priority order):
- Real-time chat latency: target 100–200ms p95 for 1:1 chat with contextual history (avg seq len ~512 tokens).
- Retrieval + reranking: currently using an embeddings-based search; want to reduce false positives and improve rerank quality for top-3 results.
- Function calling & structured outputs: output must be JSON for downstream workflow automation (orders, ETA updates).
- Cost controls: embeddings volume is significant — need batching/caching/quantization recommendations.
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 evidence and VPC/private deployment options matter for procurement.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep dive (Vivek + Dev): demo streaming + function-calling + structured output flow and discuss SDK integration changes. 60–75m.
2) Share a short PoC plan and acceptance criteria (Redwood will provide a staging model + test account).
3) Pricing/contract: we’ll prepare a draft proposal and options for Dedicated vs Hosted API (incl. estimated token + embedding spend).

Can you confirm:
- Best times for the technical deep dive next week (we’re available Tue/Thu morning PT)?
- Typical monthly embedding volume (approx vectors/month) and peak QPS for chat?

I’m attaching a short integration proposal and a technical requirements template to speed up the deep dive prep.

Attachments: redwood-integration-proposal.pdf, acme-tech-reqs.xlsx

Thanks — talk soon.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0172
From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Embeddings volume: ~2M vectors/month currently (embedding dim 768), expect growth to 5M in next 6–9 months.
- Chat QPS: peak ~40 QPS, average 8–10 QPS; typical context window ~400–600 tokens.
- Acceptable latency: p95 under 200ms is ideal for our UX.
- Compliance: SOC 2 is required; we’ll want to review audit reports. VPC/private deploy is preferred but initial PoC can use hosted with strict data controls.

Procurement timeline: aiming for contract by end of Q3; technical evaluation and security review will be the gating items.

Deep dive availability: Tue 16 Jun 9–11am PT or Thu 18 Jun 10–12pm PT. Prefer Tue if possible.

One more ask: can you show an example of structured output (function calls returning JSON) and how Redwood handles streaming partial results + re-rank pipeline? That’s the part our engineering team cares most about.

—Samir
Samir Shah
Head of Product, Acme Logistics
samir.shah@acme.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@acme.com>, Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & next steps

Thanks Samir — Tue 16 Jun 9am PT is perfect. I’ve penciled it in and sent a calendar invite to the group.

I attached the short proposal and the technical requirements spreadsheet above. Quick notes on what we’ll demo during the deep dive:
- SDK changes: show minimal-code integration (Python + JS examples) and how to wire streaming responses to a websocket front end.
- Function calling: demo structured JSON outputs for order updates and how to validate schema client-side.
- Streaming + partial function calls: show progressive tokens for the UI while final structured output is produced and how to atomically trigger downstream workflows.
- Embeddings + reranking: show sample pipeline — embed -> FAISS-like store -> candidate retrieval -> Redwood reranker (lightweight cross-encoder) for top-k re-rank.

Links for prep:
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567
- Proposal (DocuSign): https://www.docusign.com/sign/XYZ-ACME-PROPOSAL

Next actions for Acme: please fill out the attached acme-tech-reqs.xlsx with current embedding counts, example schemas for structured outputs, and any compliance questions. If you prefer, Dev can drop the answers into the doc during the technical call.

I’ve also asked our solutions engineering team (Vivek and Dev) to prepare a short demo plan and a minimal PoC checklist we can run in 2–3 weeks.

—Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Acme deep dive prep (what to demo)

Hey team —

Quick internal notes for the Tue 16 Jun deep dive with Acme (Samir/Priya):

Priority demo flow (30–40m demo + 25–30m Q&A):
1) Live chat flow (streaming): show how to stream partial tokens to the browser, maintain KV cache for context, and hit p95 latency goals.
   - Call out batching tradeoffs and how Redwood can route to a dedicated pool for predictable latency.
2) Function calling + structured outputs: show an example where the model returns a JSON payload for an "update_order" function. Demonstrate validation and error handling when schema mismatch occurs.
   - Example JSON payload (we’ll paste in demo): {"order_id": "ORD-20260501-42", "status": "in_transit", "eta_minutes": 45}
3) Embeddings + rerank: show embeddings ingestion, caching strategy, and our reranker improving top-3 precision on a small test set.
4) Cost controls & quantization: brief slide showing quantization options and expected token/embedding cost reductions.

Prep tasks (assignments):
- Vivek: prepare the streaming + function-calling demo (include JS frontend snippet and Node/Python SDK examples).
- Dev: prepare the reranker demo and a short script that shows batching and KV cache behavior for 400–600 token contexts.
- Marissa: bring negotiation points and the high-level proposal options (Hosted vs Dedicated).

Also note: Acme will want SOC 2 and VPC options. Vivek, please have our SOC 2 / security redlines doc link ready and be prepared to talk about private deployment timeline and gating items.

Attach to the HubSpot deal after the call: proposition doc + PoC checklist + tech-reqs filled.

Thanks — see you on the prep call tomorrow.

—Marissa
